newsitem.title: USA: EDnet wins financing, CEO resigns.
newsitem.headline: EDnet wins financing, CEO resigns.

text.p: EDnet Inc, a computer systems integrator and network provider, Wednesday said it has secured new long-term equity financing leading to the resignation of Chief Executive Officer Chuck Erickson.
In a statement, the company said Erickson is being replaced by Tom Kobayashi, founder chairman and former chief executive.

EDnet also estimated revenues for its fiscal year ended June 30, 1997 should be 50 percent above fiscal 1996's $2.53 million, due largely to significant second half growth in its "network usage" business, demand for its unique network bridging service and rising Internet web design business.
Also resigning from EDnet's board are Trevor Stout, Phil Ramone and Jack Kraft. Charles Clark, senior parter of DeWitt Wolf Consultants LLC will join the board.

DeWitt Wolf was appointed financial advisor after helping to raise nearly $4.0 million in equity financing for the company. Moreover, DeWitt has completed an agreement with the company's major noteholders that will allow it to restructure its balance sheet, EDnet said.
EDnet said the financing and a restructured balance sheet will help it focus on increasing demand for its core networking business and move forward with possible acquisitions.
